subject: €13 billion in defence contracts, "substantial irregularities" in the paperwork
publicRecord: In a report approved on 14 September 2022, the Belgian Court of Audit (Rekenhof / Cour des comptes) examined how the Ministry of Defence awards public contracts. It found that Defence awarded more than €13 billion in contracts (excluding VAT) between 2018 and 2020. That €13 billion is the total value of contracts awarded, not a loss and not an overrun. The control framework was 'reasonably well developed', but the audit flagged substantial regularity shortcomings: weak application of the competition and equal-treatment rules on smaller contracts, and insufficient scrutiny of bidders' prices on larger ones. This is an audit-regularity finding, not a finding of criminal wrongdoing.

subject: €2.5 billion on external consultants in three years, most of it inadequately justified
publicRecord: A Belgian Court of Audit report, reported on 12 November 2025, found that the federal government spent about €2.5 billion on external consultants over 2020-2022, roughly €2 billion of it on IT. The Court found that 78.22% of the contracts it examined lacked proper justification and 44.55% carried unrealistic cost estimates, and it cited one contract estimated at €400,000 that ultimately cost €10 million. The Court described the weaknesses as 'structural'. This is an audit finding on spending controls, not a finding of criminal wrongdoing.

subject: €14.5 billion Flemish road and infrastructure maintenance backlog
publicRecord: A Court of Audit (Rekenhof) audit of Flanders' Integrated Investment Programme (GIP), reported on 18 June 2026, put the region's infrastructure maintenance backlog at about €14.5 billion, needing roughly €1.45 billion a year for ten years to clear. It found that a promised €530 million of extra 2025 investment came to €363 million in practice, and criticised that more than 150 projects were added on political grounds without objective scoring, with the roads agency warning it could not rule out safety-related closures of lanes, tunnels or bridges. This is an audit finding, not an allegation of wrongdoing.

subject: Walloon direct debt projected at €32.8 billion, accounts not certifiable
publicRecord: In its 37th cahier of observations to the Walloon Parliament (28 October 2025), the Court of Audit (Cour des comptes) documented Wallonia's rising regional debt, including direct-debt interest charges of €471.7 million in 2024, up from €344.1 million in 2023. As reported by RTBF from the same cahier, the Court projected Wallonia's direct regional debt at about €32.8 billion by the end of 2026. The Court reported that many receivables and the Region's property portfolio are not properly inventoried or valued, which prevents it from certifying a true-and-fair view of the accounts, and it flagged weaknesses in public-procurement procedures. These are audit observations, not findings of criminal wrongdoing.

subject: €462.6 million, 28-year contract to renovate Brussels' longest tunnel
publicRecord: The renovation of the Leopold II tunnel in Brussels (renamed the Annie Cordy tunnel), Belgium's longest urban tunnel, was awarded to the Circul2020 consortium as a design-build-finance-maintain contract worth €462.6 million over 28 years, including about €264.7 million for the renovation works and about €180.3 million for 25 years of maintenance. The overall cost of the project was later reported at around €512 million, roughly €50 million above the initial contract figure. These are contract and reported-cost figures for the tunnel, not audited overruns or established losses.
